purpose: T0.3: does subgrid sizing drive FOGGIE's load imbalance? Tests the audit's recommendation AND the opposite direction.

config.note: 4 arms run concurrently on separate nodes; node scatter ~1.6% against effects of 24-70%.

build: ee9d6d10f3f3 (no code change - pure parameter experiment)
headline: Arm C is 24% faster than control (1715.9 vs 2260.0 s) with the barrier down 46% (1418.9 -> 763.9 s). Perfectly monotonic in grid count: more, smaller grids -> better balance -> less barrier -> less wall.
audit_recommendation_INVERTED: The audit's T0.3 (arm B) is 70% SLOWER. Its rationale - per-grid overhead and O(S^2) sibling searches - predates T1.9, which removed the sibling cost. Recommend the OPPOSITE direction.

why_it_works.granularity: L10 has 195 grids over 128 ranks = 1.52 grids/rank, with sizes 24-15552 cells (648x spread). Fair share is 846880/128 = 6616 cells, so the largest single grid is 2.35x a fair share and is INDIVISIBLE - no balancer of any kind can fix that. Measured per-subcycle max/mean work is 2.71x, matching.
why_it_works.second_effect: Smaller boxes fit the flagged region more tightly, so less unflagged padding gets refined: total active cells at L>=8 drop 2,675,416 -> 2,270,288 (-15%). Flagged cells remain covered, so this is efficiency, not lost resolution.

root_cause_in_code: DetermineSubgridSizeExtrema already computes the right answer - NumberOfCells/(NumberOfProcessors*OptimalSubgridsPerProcessor) = 846880/(128*16) = 413 cells, essentially arm C - and then throws it away via max(413, MINIMUM_SIZE) with a hard-coded '#define MINIMUM_SIZE 2000'. That constant predates high core counts and is the actual defect.
headroom_remaining: A cap of 400 should give ~2117 grids at L10; only 436 appeared (~20% of theoretical). ProtoSubgrid_AcceptableGrid rejects oversized grids, but Berger-Rigoutsos splits on signature zero-crossings and a SOLIDLY flagged region (the galaxy centre) has no feature to split on. Forced/geometric bisection when oversized - the audit's T2.10 - is now a quantified opportunity.

correctness.result: Conserved quantities conserved: baryon 5.9e-10, dark matter 9.3e-16 (machine precision). Star formation differs: 1,423,057 vs 1,421,808 stars (-0.088%), stellar mass 1.3e-3.
correctness.self_consistency: The 1249 missing stars leave their gas baryonic: stellar deficit 8.5e-11 absolute against baryon total 0.1618 predicts a baryon excess of 5.3e-10; measured 5.9e-10. The books balance.
correctness.IMPORTANT: These numbers required fixing compare_runs.py (commit 92e436d0). The previous metric reported baryon 9.6e-3 and DM 2.4e-2, which are impossible - DM particle counts are bit-identical at 19,195,353. It had no cell volume, no particle dx^3, and double-counted refined regions. Same-structure (C0/C1) verdicts are unaffected because the errors cancel there.

recommendation: Do NOT hard-code MaximumSubgridSize=400 in the production deck - it is anchored to this problem size and rank count. Make MINIMUM_SIZE a parameter defaulting to 2000, so DetermineSubgridSizeExtrema's existing adaptive formula is honoured at any rank count. Then re-measure.
